title: SS27 Kids' Woven Fabric Direction
summary: Lightweight linen, voile, organic cotton poplin, gingham and diverse denim lead SS27 kidswear wovens, with recycled and certified materials.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body: Collections increasingly use recycled fibres, organic cotton and certified materials<sup>[1]</sup>. Fatamadrina lists lightweight linen, voile and organic cotton, with gingham among SS27 prints<sup>[2]</sup>. Denim was "stronger and more diverse than in recent seasons" at Playtime Paris<sup>[3]</sup>. Marie Raxevisky uses fine Italian fabrics and recycled materials<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Fabric by fabric
sections.body:
| Fabric | Hand | Uses |
|---|---|---|
| Organic cotton poplin | Crisp, light | Shirts, dresses |
| Linen and linen-cotton | Cool, textured | Shirts, shorts, dresses |
| Voile | Very light | Dresses, blouses, layers |
| Gingham cotton | Light | Dresses, shirts |
| Denim, light to mid weight | Durable | Dungarees, jackets, shorts |
| Twill | Firm | Shorts, trousers |

design_implications:
- Pre-wash linen and denim to control shrinkage.
- Certify organic claims (for example GOTS) before using them.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist of young children's clothing, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, beads, shells and other decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
commercial_implications: - Organic cotton and linen support a premium; denim is volume.
